object_description: Four rectangular volumes united by touching roofs around a central garden
design_condition: The single-storey pavilion is positioned between the road and the bottom of the slope, with its four volumes creating a protected central garden and clearly separated exterior sectors.

positive.statement: The axial volumetric composition forms a beautiful and neutral wooden pavilion.
The dimensions allow the children's life center to be skillfully positioned between the road and the bottom of the slope.
The private and protected central garden unifies the house and avoids restrictive fencing around the surrounding spaces.
The four volumes generate a generous garden space at the center.
The touching roofs cleverly form a single object while preserving permeability.
The distribution choices are logical and integrate the parameters and uses of the site.
The daring approach ensures short and undivided routes.
Centralized entrances open directly onto changing rooms and make distribution very easy.
The project is credible and constructively realistic, with provision for a possible second floor.
The project has great coherence in location, organization and identity in relation to the world of childhood.
The rational and efficient timber structure provides economy and low spans for gravity loads.
The symmetrical vertical supporting systems provide excellent dynamic behavior during an earthquake.
The single-level construction is relevant for poor soil and may save deep foundations.
The proposed extension offers great flexibility for future needs.
The materials support durability, sustainable development and savings in gray energy.
Fire quality assurance aspects are well resolved.
